rooms.question: Does aiming higher always send a launch farther?
rooms.ontology: A launch velocity has horizontal and vertical components. Gravity changes the vertical component over time, so the initial direction and the resulting curved path are different things.
rooms.action: Move the ANGLE slider and compare the traced arc, its apex and landing marker. Find a low and a high angle with similar range while the launch power stays fixed.
rooms.observable: A steeper direction increases the upward share but reduces the horizontal share. Range grows and then shrinks; complementary directions can land at the same horizontal distance by different paths.
rooms.mechanism: LaunchArc._build_demo calculates vx=v0*cos(theta), vy=v0*sin(theta), landing time=2*vy/g, then draws a stroboscopic parabola. ToyConsole._on_slider_moved rebuilds the model as angle changes from22° to70°. This is a parameter-controlled static diagram, not a launcher that fires the player.
rooms.limit: The range relationship assumes fixed gravity, no air resistance and landing at launch height. The displayed trace does not demonstrate collision, wind or steering during flight.
rooms.variation: Choose a high route and a low route to the same landing and compare which would clear an imagined obstacle. An actual obstacle test would require a separate launch simulation.
rooms.cautions: Do not follow the identity header’s claim that this specific toy throws the visitor. Power is a configuration value; only ANGLE is a visitor slider.

rooms.question: How can a continuous adjustment produce a sudden start?
rooms.ontology: A force balance can hold a body still until a threshold is crossed. The component of gravity along a slope competes with a friction bound set by the normal component.
rooms.action: Keep the ramp angle fixed and move μ until the block changes between STATIC and SLIDING. Then hold μ fixed and vary ANGLE. Use RESET to compare fresh runs.
rooms.observable: The labels and force arrows change as the block begins to move. Below the threshold the model holds the block; above it the displayed velocity accumulates and the block accelerates down the ramp.
rooms.mechanism: _update_physics_state compares sin(theta) with μ*cos(theta). When sliding it sets acceleration=g*(sin(theta)−μ*cos(theta)); _physics_process adds acceleration*delta to velocity and velocity*delta to slope position, scaled for display. It automatically resets at the bottom.
rooms.limit: The model uses one coefficient and a simplified state switch, whereas real contacts may distinguish static and kinetic friction and have more complex material behavior. No movement is not evidence of no forces.
rooms.variation: Approach the threshold from each side and compare the displayed decision. A separate static/kinetic coefficient pair would be a proposed extension capable of demonstrating hysteresis.
rooms.cautions: Runtime access and controls require a museum walk; source-read only.

rooms.question: If two collisions conserve the same kind of quantity, must their outcomes look alike?
rooms.ontology: Momentum combines mass with signed velocity. Conservation constrains the sum, while the distribution of velocity between bodies can change.
rooms.action: Move MASS RATIO on the collision-carts console. Compare the upper before lane with the lower after lane: track the striker’s arrow as it reverses, disappears near equal masses, and points forward for a heavier striker.
rooms.observable: Changing the mass ratio changes both outgoing arrows. A light striker rebounds, equal masses transfer the incoming motion in this model, and a heavy striker continues forward while the other cart leaves faster.
rooms.mechanism: _build_demo fixes target mass at1 and initial striker speed at1. It evaluates the one-dimensional elastic collision formulas vA=(mA−mB)/(mA+mB)*u and vB=2*mA/(mA+mB)*u, then draws separate before/after lanes. The console slider rebuilds those static comparison diagrams.
rooms.limit: This is an ideal elastic, isolated, one-dimensional comparison, not a live collision arena. Arrow lengths include a visual minimum, so their lengths are not an exact ruler for measuring momentum.
rooms.variation: Predict the sign of the striker’s outgoing velocity before moving through equal masses. A sticky collision would conserve momentum with a different energy result, but no restitution control is available on this console.
rooms.cautions: There are many broader active arena encounters in this developed room. This is a focused initial book route only; retain them as secondary and record later expansion rather than remove them.
